{{Short description|Russian mathematician and educator}}
[[File:Monument in honor of Leonty Magnitsky in the city Ostashkov.JPG|thumb|Monument in honor of Magnitsky in Ostashkov]]
'''Leonty Filippovich Magnitsky''' ({{langx|ru|Леонтий Филиппович Магницкий}}), born '''Telyatin''' ({{langx|ru|Телятин}}; June 9, 1669, in [[Ostashkov]] – October 19, 1739, in [[Moscow]]) was a Russian [[mathematician]] and [[educator]].<ref name="treadgold">{{citation|title=The West in Russia and China: Russia, 1472–1917|first=Donald W.|last=Treadgold|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=1973|isbn=9780521097253|page=86|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Fg04AAAAIAAJ&pg=PA86}}.</ref>

== Biography ==
Magnitsky was born into a peasant family. According to some accounts, he graduated from the [[Slavic Greek Latin Academy]] in Moscow.<ref name="treadgold"/> From 1701 and until his death, he taught [[arithmetic]], [[geometry]] and [[trigonometry]] at the [[Moscow School of Mathematics and Navigation]], becoming its director in 1716.

In 1703, Magnitsky wrote his famous ''[[Arithmetic (book)|Arithmetic]]'' (Арифметика; 2,400 copies), which was used as the principal textbook on mathematics in Russia until the middle of the 18th century.<ref name="treadgold"/> [[Mikhail Lomonosov]] was himself taught by this book,<ref>{{citation|title=Russian Literature|first1=Andrew Baruch|last1=Wachtel|first2=Ilya|last2=Vinitsky|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|year=2013|isbn=9780745654577|page=52|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BWHAWGmJxpYC&pg=PT52}}.</ref> which he called the "gates to his own erudition".<ref>{{citation|title=Icon and Axe: An Interpretative History of Russian Culture|first=James|last=Billington|publisher=Random House LLC|year=2010|isbn=9780307765284|pages=289–290|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Oc6ILm2SFI8C&pg=PT289–290}}.</ref> In 1703, Magnitsky also produced a Russian edition of [[Adriaan Vlacq]]'s log tables called ''Таблицы логарифмов и синусов, тангенсов и секансов'' (Tables of [[logarithm]]s, [[sine]]s, [[tangent]]s, and [[Trigonometric functions#Reciprocal functions|secants]]{{Broken anchor|date=2024-09-29|bot=User:Cewbot/log/20201008/configuration|target_link=Trigonometric functions#Reciprocal functions|reason= The anchor (Reciprocal functions) [[Special:Diff/779343428|has been deleted]].}}).

Legend has it that Leonty Magnitsky was nicknamed ''Magnitsky'' by [[Peter the Great]], who considered him a "people's [[magnet]]" (магнит, or "magnit" in Russian). For his educatorial achievements he was ennobled in 1704, and was given numerous awards and gifts by the Tsar.
